name: Ridge & Valley Roofing
oneLiner: Re-roofing and roof plumbing for weather that means it — built square, flashed right, guaranteed in writing.
axisNote: second brutalist-raw exercise after Crateline, distinct by construction: Crateline's brutalism is BUREAUCRATIC (waybills, ledgers, stamps); Ridge & Valley's is MATERIAL (the page is built like a roof — ridge rules open every chapter, columns split along valley channels, spec plates are stamped into surfaces, zero border-radius anywhere — the portfolio's only fully square site). The cinematic secondary is the weather: a storm arrives over the scroll and the minted storm/material photography carries the emotional register.
paletteSeed: zinc-white paper and near-black ink under a sky that changes: clear noon zinc → bruised storm teal-charcoal → burst → washed golden evening; ONE loud accent, terracotta oxide, for actions and stamps; storm teal belongs to the sky only, never to UI
typeDirection: Barlow Condensed 700 (poster display — DIN/roadside-signage DNA, the trade's own letterform tradition) + Barlow 400/600 (body, same family: brutalist one-family discipline) + Fragment Mono (spec plates, the gauge) — all OFL, vendored, all portfolio-new
motionBudget: one scroll clock: THE STORM — the fixed sky layer darkens toward the storm-test chapter and resolves to gold at the close; a code-drawn storm gauge (mm/h rain, km/h gusts climbing toward the stated wind rating) runs beside a code-drawn roof cross-section that sheds the same storm (rain streaks, water line running the pitch to the gutter, pulsing downpipe); the wink is a blue emergency tarp pinned over one card at peak ('temporary fix — book the permanent one'); no-JS/reduced-motion = the complete page with the sky as static per-chapter bands, the gauge at peak reading, the rain as still texture, the tarp visible
